messages:
kevin: Quick heads up — noticed a routing anomaly when clients send `X-Region-Prefer`. Some requests that should prefer eu-west are landing in us-east when latency is within ~10ms.
sara: Can you paste an example request + current route config? curious if it's header parsing or the hash fallback.
kevin: repro snippet:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.com
X-Region-Prefer: eu-west
X-Client-IP: 35.198.2.4
```
routing rule: prefer header -> hash(client_ip) -> latency probe fallback
but behavior looks like header is ignored for ~5% of flows.
maria: any chance header case mismatch or whitespace? the nginx/envoy layer lowercases headers, but our gateway has a header-normalization step too.
anil: could also be the 'prefer' semantics. We currently treat `X-Region-Prefer` as a soft hint (weight 0.7) not a hard override. If latency diff < threshold we apply hashing rules. That's intended but maybe too aggressive.
kevin: yes i dug in — we treat prefer as weight 0.7. for some tenants their traffic has short tail latency so it picks local hash destination. the issue is we don't attach telemetry about "why" we chose a region.
sara: proposal: change semantics to
- `X-Region-Prefer: <region>` defaults to strong hint (0.95) for customers that set `force=false`
- add `X-Region-Force: 1` to make it sticky/hard override
- normalize header names and trim values server-side
also: tag telemetry with `route.choice_reason` = ["header_force","header_hint","latency_hash","quota_evict"]
maria: i'm +1 on telemetry tagging. ops need to see reason in traces and per-route dashboards :eyes:
anil: also add a config knob on route: `latency_sensitivity` (0..1) so product teams can trade cost/latency. default remains 0.3 but can be bumped per-tenant.
kevin: will need to update gateway docs and console UX for rollout (a toggle to prefer/force region). plan: canary change header semantics for 5% traffic next week, surface new `route.choice_reason` in console traces, then 50% after smoke tests.
ops-bot: deploy started for service=api-gateway env=staging commit=ab12cd :rocket:
sara: another gotcha — quotas: if tenant has reserved dedicated capacity in eu-west, header prefer should not override capacity rules. order of precedence: capacity/quotas -> force header -> hint header -> hash -> latency. confirm?
maria: yes quotas and capacity must always win. add unit test for precedence.
kevin: ok i'll open a PR with code and tests, and add a migration that lowercases header keys in gateway. PR will include changelog for console and docs. sgtm? :thumbsup:
anil: sgtm — add a telemetry flag to gate high-volume traces during canary (sample by route.choice_reason)
kevin: thanks — will post PR link when ready and schedule the canary this Thursday 09:00 UTC.
